title: One logical update and replayed block activations
description: Keep target normalization, optimizer timing, dropout replay and the retained-payload observation distinct.

terms.definition: The examples whose valid next-token targets define one combined mean loss and one optimizer update. The caller chooses this group; splitting it into microbatches does not add optimizer steps.
A smaller part of a logical batch processed by its own forward and backward pass. Release that graph before the next microbatch while keeping model weights and the logical update's loss scale fixed.

Add each microbatch mean-loss gradient in proportion to its valid-target count divided by the logical group's total. Padding is excluded. Equal averaging of microbatch means changes the token objective when their valid counts differ.

After every microbatch succeeds, unscale the combined gradient, measure its global norm, apply existing clipping and run AdamW once. Clear gradients and advance the loss-scale controller once. A later failed microbatch discards partial model gradients before this finish phase.

In graph-recording training, retain block boundaries and a replay recipe instead of the block's interior tape, then repeat its forward calculation during backward. This adds computation; an activation checkpoint is temporary derivative state, not a saved model-weight file.

A compact record that regenerates one dropout site's original random choices. Block replay keeps the same layout and exact site ranges without advancing a live random counter. A seed alone does not preserve per-token masks after changing microbatch shapes or padding.

The chapter's after-forward count for the tape reachable from the scalar mean-loss node: nonparameter primals, owned saved-context tensors and fixed checkpoint-recipe tensors in f64 bytes. Include copied parameter primals in saved contexts; exclude original parameter, gradient and optimizer buffers, metadata, layout and tickets, capacity and transient work. It is neither total nor peak training memory, process memory or GPU storage.
